title: A Declarative Optimization Engine for Resource Provisioning of Scientific Workflows in Geo-Distributed Clouds
central_claims: Geco provides declarative specification and probabilistic optimization for geo-distributed workflow provisioning.
GPU acceleration and runtime optimization improve cost/performance across four provisioning problems.

source_manifest.title: A Declarative Optimization Engine for Resource Provisioning of Scientific Workflows in Geo-Distributed Clouds
source_manifest.finding: Author institution reproduces original abstract: Geco combines declarative goals, probabilistic evaluation, runtime optimization and GPU acceleration.

source_manifest.title: Taming System Dynamics on Resource Optimization for Data Processing Workflows: A Probabilistic Approach
source_manifest.finding: Overlapping authors develop Prob for workflow variability; original authorship overlap prevents treating its experiments as independent validation of Geco.

answers.rationale: No independent primary experiment confirming the Geco cost/performance claims was retrieved.
No independent implementation or reproduction of the journal version was identified; Deco is a distinct earlier contribution.
The accessible later probabilistic study shares original authors and does not supply independent testing of Geco.
No read authoritative assessment explicitly retaining the journal paper’s central claim was found.
No follow-up testing of Geco’s specific limitations was verified; full original limitations were inaccessible.
Related Prob and privacy-scheduling papers share authors, so they cannot establish independent extension.
Two independent groups substantively building on Geco were not documented.
Search results for independent workflow papers commonly concern the earlier Deco system; actual Geco reuse was not established.
No independent review explicitly attributes a new research direction to the geo-distributed journal contribution.
No independent benchmark using Geco as a tested baseline was verified.
No independent application demonstrates a scientific or practical benefit specifically attributable to Geco.
Success outside the four original provisioning problems was not verified.
The later Prob contribution is related, but its accessible text does not establish that the journal Geco result enabled a new capability.
No public deployment or operational workflow using Geco was documented.
No independent comparison establishes retained cost, speed or performance advantages of Geco.
Post-2019 related work exists, but substantive use of this journal contribution was not verified.
No positive independent assessment after August 2019 was found for Geco’s central claims.
Two calendar years of substantive independent Geco follow-up were not documented.
Retrieved workflow synthesis leads discuss the earlier Deco paper; adoption of the journal contribution by a synthesis remains unverified.
No source demonstrates continued usefulness of Geco relative to newer workflow schedulers.

search_gaps: Original journal full text could not be obtained from DOI, institutional record or author publication pages. The accessible 2015 Deco PDF is not substituted for the 2016 Geco journal paper.

A later independent container-scheduling PDF citing the original was located but fetching its body failed; a citation alone was not counted as uptake. Named-method searches repeatedly returned unrelated Geco systems.
research.summary: Geco’s identity and reported claims are established from its abstract. Accessible related follow-up is largely shared-author research or concerns the earlier Deco version; independent outcomes remain unverified.
